assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative data changed how mobility is measured. It documented large geographic variation, showed that childhood place exerts causal effects, and produced open, reusable data. The findings have informed policy and follow-on research across fields. The design is transparent and robust to scrutiny, which I weight heavily.
assessment.attribution: Chetty is central and Hendren and Friedman are close collaborators on the core mobility and neighborhood-effects papers. Lawrence Katz (Moving to Opportunity) is an important contributor but is outside the three-name limit. Chetty's wider work also appears in B001, so the credit is partly shared across candidates.
assessment.maturity: The work spans roughly 2014 to 2022. Many findings have been replicated or extended in other countries and datasets, and policy uptake is visible. Maturity is adequate but not as deep as for older candidates.
uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers to recognise Chetty through this topic or through public finance (B001).
Causal interpretation of the neighborhood-exposure estimates rests on identifying assumptions that remain debated.
The three-person limit excludes Katz.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work covers the task-based view of technology and labour demand, and the China trade shock's local labour-market effects. Together these reshaped understanding of wage inequality, polarisation and the distributional costs of trade. It matters for current debates on automation and AI. The empirical designs are clear and widely replicated.
assessment.attribution: Autor is the unifying figure across the tasks and trade-shock literatures. Hanson and Dorn are core co-authors of the China shock papers. Lawrence Katz, Levy, Murnane and Acemoglu contributed to the tasks framework, so credit is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: The tasks framework dates from the early 2000s and the China shock papers from 2013 to 2021. There has been extensive follow-up, some of it qualifying the magnitudes of the effects.
uncertainties: Recent laureates (Acemoglu, Johnson, Robinson; Goldin) are adjacent in topic.
Persistence and magnitude of the China shock effects are debated.
The tasks credit overlaps with people outside this candidate's names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity transformed trade theory and empirics. It explains selection, exporter premia and new channels for gains from trade. It also underlies a large body of micro-data work. The theoretical contribution is foundational and has been tested extensively.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the clear seminal paper. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to FDI and trade margins and has a long record in new trade theory. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are important contributors outside this candidate's credited names, which makes attribution contested. Redding is a later contributor, so I exclude him.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of testing. Core predictions on selection and productivity are supported, with refinements on welfare formulas.
uncertainties: Possible need to include Bernard, Eaton and Jensen, who are not listed here.
Krugman's 2008 prize partly covers adjacent ground.
Welfare implications depend on functional-form assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification formalises what can be credibly concluded under weak assumptions and confronts the credibility cost of unsupported assumptions. This has methodological value across applied fields. I give weight to its direct relevance to research credibility, but I flag that this is a personal affinity.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the originator of bounds and the identification framework. Tamer made central contributions to moment inequalities and set inference. Molinari is also important but is excluded by the cap.
assessment.maturity: The foundations date from the late 1980s and 1990s, with extensive subsequent development. Applied adoption is real but narrower than for design-based methods.
uncertainties: Practical influence on applied practice is more limited than that of competing methods.
Credit division among Manski, Tamer, Molinari and others is uncertain.
Econometric methods were recently honoured (2021).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Social preferences established, through experiments and theory, that fairness, reciprocity and costly punishment shape behaviour in games and contracts. Inequity aversion models gave tractable formalisation. The topic is of broad importance for behavioural economics. Core experimental findings replicated well in large replication efforts, which strengthens my confidence.
assessment.attribution: Fehr is the leading empirical and conceptual figure. Fehr and Schmidt (1999) is the key theory paper, with Bolton and Ockenfels (2000) as a parallel model outside the credited names. Falk, Gächter and Rabin are significant contributors, so credit is spread across many people.
assessment.maturity: Developed since the 1990s and thoroughly tested. Field relevance and some boundary conditions remain contested.
uncertainties: Possible omission of Bolton and Ockenfels, Gächter or Rabin.
External validity of lab-measured preferences for field behaviour.
My own field proximity may bias my assessment upward.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run top-income and wealth series built from tax data transformed the measurement of inequality and shaped global policy debate. The measurement contribution is substantial and has been widely extended through the World Inequality Database. Interpretive claims, such as the r>g dynamics, are more contested than the data work.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez established top-income series, and Zucman extended them to wealth and offshore holdings. Atkinson, now deceased, was a major pioneer. Saez also appears in B001.
assessment.maturity: Time series work dates from 2003, with offshore wealth work in the 2010s. Impact is large, but methodological debates over distributional accounts continue.
uncertainties: Disputes over imputation methods and treatment of pensions and transfers.
Dispute over how much weight the theoretical claims carry relative to measurement.
Credit overlap with Atkinson's legacy and with B001.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The framework links micro-level misallocation of inputs to aggregate TFP differences across countries and offers a quantitative account of income gaps. It has driven a large literature in development and macro and has had policy influence. The measurement approach has strengths but depends on model structure.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the seminal paper and is clearly jointly credited. Restuccia and Rogerson and others shaped the broader misallocation agenda but sit outside the cap.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of follow-up. Measurement concerns, such as measurement error in firm data and the interpretation of wedges, remain active.
uncertainties: Sensitivity of measured misallocation to measurement error and functional-form assumptions.
Overlap with 2025 growth-prize themes.
Credit split with Restuccia, Rogerson and others.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work showed with granular micro data that household debt expansions and credit supply shocks help explain the housing boom, the Great Recession's depth and slow recovery. It reoriented macro-finance toward household balance sheets. The empirical approach is mostly credible, though some conclusions about credit supply versus other channels remain debated.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear joint originators of the key papers and the House of Debt synthesis. Campbell contributed to related household finance research but is a weaker fit for this particular discovery.
assessment.maturity: The core evidence dates from about 2009 to 2018. It is influential but younger than other candidates, and the 2022 prize covered adjacent crisis topics.
uncertainties: Competing evidence on the role of credit supply versus expectations and fraud.
Prior recognition of crisis-related work (2022) may reduce priority.
Replication of the main findings in other countries is mixed.
